solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hurry up Tom, otherwise the other Jack will go ahead

indicators.note: will go ahead means the jack letter is placed in front of everything else

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters of up and Tom are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
'the other' is a coy phrase for sex, as is IT

explanation.surface: Someone urging Tom to get a move on before the other Jack beats him to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hurry up' reads as the definition, but 'up' belongs to the anagram fodder that 'otherwise' shuffles; 'will go ahead' puts the card letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an order to get moving at once, so it amounts to telling someone to hurry.

clue.text: Reversal of extremely unjust run-out

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, first and last, of unjust
out signals the letters of run are put out of order

explanation.surface: A cricketer complains that a run-out decision was a grossly unfair overturning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes U and T from 'unjust'; 'out' rearranges RUN as URN.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete about-turn, literal on the road or figurative in policy, is a reversal.

clue.text: In butterfly, gasped to catch international youth before end of relay

indicators.note: to catch means the panting word holds the international letter inside it

parts.note: gasped means panted
a youth is a lad

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of relay

explanation.surface: A swimmer in the butterfly leg, out of breath, is overtaken by a young international before the relay ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In butterfly' sounds like a swimming stroke; butterfly is the insect being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common orange-and-black species of butterfly found worldwide.

clue.text: Best not batting given what bowlers may do to the ball

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who is no longer batting is out

parts.words: what bowlers may do to the ball
parts.note: cricket bowlers polish one side of the ball on their trousers to make it swing, called shining it

explanation.surface: A cricket line about a dismissed batsman and the bowlers polishing the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Best is a verb here, meaning to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone, to be brighter or better than them, is to best them.

clue.text: Could this yield tense, close-up photos captured by crew?

definitions.text: Could this yield tense, close-up photos captured by crew?

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: captured by means the following letters sit inside the crew word

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

indicators.note: up means in disarray, so the letters of close are mixed

parts.note: pics is short for pictures, i.e. photos

explanation.surface: Asking whether a gun scope could take tense close-up shots of a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close-up' splits: 'up' is the anagram signal for 'close' alone, and 'captured by' places the result inside the rowing crew, so the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifying scope mounted on a rifle brings distant targets close, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Official you heard quietly entering bog

indicators.note: heard means the word you is taken as it is spoken, as one letter

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

indicators.note: entering means the quiet letter goes inside the bog word

parts.note: a mire is a bog
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: An official overheard sinking quietly into a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives U from 'you'; 'entering' puts P inside MIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A match official, as in cricket or tennis, who rules on play.

clue.text: Consequence of having risen dramatically following exchange

indicators.note: following an exchange, the two halves of the phrase swap places

parts.note: something that has risen dramatically has shot up

explanation.surface: Prices that soared after a trade, and what came of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following exchange' swaps the two words of SHOT UP.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or result of events is a consequence.

clue.text: By George, Napoleon is spying intermittently

definitions.note: in George Orwell's Animal Farm, Napoleon is the tyrant boar

indicators.note: intermittently means every other letter of spying is taken

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at Napoleon being caught spying now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By George' is not an exclamation: it means written by George Orwell, whose Napoleon is a boar.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's farm fable Napoleon is a boar who seizes control, so he is a swine.

clue.text: Bar admitting adult manner when having to contend with animated account of trip?

indicators.note: admitting means the bar word lets the adult letter in

parts.note: a rod is a bar
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
MO, modus operandi, is a way or manner of working
to vie is to contend

explanation.surface: A pub lets in a grown-up who must cope with a lively retelling of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated account' suggests a cartoon, but means a film, a moving picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A film genre about a journey, so a moving-picture story of a trip.

clue.text: Non-British artist embracing English potter?

indicators.note: embracing means the trimmed artist holds the English letter inside
non-British means the B for British is removed

parts.note: a cubist is an artist such as Picasso

explanation.surface: A foreign painter holding an English ceramicist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potter' suggests ceramics, but in snooker and billiards to pot is to sink a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiards or snooker player pots balls with a cue, so is a potter in a whimsical sense.

clue.text: When in Los Angeles, celebrated about Mediterranean dishes

indicators.note: in means the when word goes inside the Los Angeles abbreviation

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: about means the celebrated word is turned round

parts.note: to sing of someone is to celebrate them, so sang is celebrated

explanation.surface: Visiting Los Angeles, someone hymns the praises of Mediterranean food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When in Los Angeles' looks like scene-setting; 'in' is an instruction, and 'about' turns the celebrated word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered pasta bakes from Italy, a Mediterranean country, are classic Mediterranean dishes.

clue.text: Kick over fly

indicators.note: over means the kick word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a tang is a sharp flavour, a kick

explanation.surface: An instruction to swat a fly by kicking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TANG back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A small two-winged biting insect is a kind of fly.

clue.text: That guy's turn to stop Sting coming back in charts

parts.note: his means belonging to that guy

indicators.note: coming back means the whole stinging part is read backwards
to stop means the turn word plugs a gap inside the sting word

parts.note: to smart is to sting
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A man takes his turn to block the singer Sting's return to the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting is not the singer but a verb; 'to stop' plugs the turn into it before 'coming back' reverses the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar charts showing frequencies are statistical diagrams of this type.

clue.text: Mention pinching outfit? Soldier's in the cooler?

indicators.note: pinching means the mention word grips the outfit word inside it

parts.note: to refer to something is to mention it
a rig is an outfit of clothes
a soldier ant is a worker type; the apostrophe-s is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone mentions an outfit being stolen and a soldier being in the jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cooler' looks like slang for prison, but means a substance that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical used in a fridge to absorb heat is what does the cooling.

clue.text: Dance judge shunned by cool jazz guitarist

parts.note: to fan someone is to cool them

indicators.note: shunned by means the judge letter is kept out of the guitarist's name

parts.note: Django Reinhardt was a celebrated jazz guitarist

explanation.surface: A dance judge snubbed by a laid-back jazz musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance judge' looks like a phrase, but 'judge' is just its letter, which 'shunned by' takes out of the guitarist's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Spanish dance in triple time, performed with castanets.

clue.text: Faux-fur shrank at start of airing after being spun

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of airing
being spun suggests a tumble in a washer, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A fake fur coat that shrank in the wash before being aired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after being spun' covers all three pieces: 'start of' supplies the airing letter, which joins the anagram rather than sitting outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is used for a fabric with a curled pile made to imitate lambskin, a faux fur.

clue.text: Pet's fine farewell

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
ave is Latin for hail or farewell

explanation.surface: Saying a fine goodbye to a beloved animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet's' reads as a possessive but is 'Pet is'; pet is a favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is a favourite person or thing, and the slang shortening means just that.

clue.text: Camel germs inviting loss of energy followed by onset of nausea

indicators.note: inviting loss of means the germ word drops the energy letter

parts.note: bacteria are germs
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: onset of picks the first letter of nausea

explanation.surface: A camel's germs drain its energy and bring on sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inviting loss of' takes E from BACTERIA, leaving BACTRIA; 'onset of' adds N.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-humped beast of Central Asia is the Bactrian camel.

clue.text: Mountain in which petunia is picked in prime locations

indicators.note: only letters at prime-numbered positions (second, third, fifth, seventh) are kept, so the first, fourth and sixth go

explanation.surface: A mountainside where a petunia is chosen from the best spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime locations' sounds like choice sites but means positions 2, 3, 5 and 7 of 'petunia'.
explanation.definitionFit: The active volcano in eastern Sicily is a famous mountain.

clue.text: Thought picture should frame fashionable duke

indicators.note: should frame means the picture word surrounds the fashionable word

parts.note: an image is a picture
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a portrait ought to frame a stylish duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should frame' is the containment signal, with the picture holding the fashionable word.
explanation.definitionFit: To have pictured something in the mind is to have thought it up.

clue.text: Genial sweetheart needs drug bottle

parts.note: jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart
a vial is a small bottle for medicine

explanation.surface: A cheerful sweetheart in need of a medicine bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: JO, a sweetheart in old Scots, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and cheerful in manner is a close synonym of good-humoured and genial.

clue.text: Convenient new diet, so take your time

parts.note: easy means convenient, presenting no difficulty

indicators.note: new means the letters of diet and so form a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice that a handy new diet should be followed slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DIET SO into DOES IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges going gently and carefully, i.e. not rushing.

clue.text: Formerly understood only the core elements

indicators.note: only the core elements means the middle letters of understood are kept, three trimmed at each end

explanation.surface: Something once grasped only in its essentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only the core elements' keeps the middle four letters of 'understood'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning at an earlier time, as in its longer form erstwhile.

clue.text: Note raised by small instrument

parts.note: a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musical note played on a tiny instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: A note raised by a semitone is marked with this sign.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a note pitched a semitone higher is so called.

clue.text: Light-fingered devil exposed in affair

indicators.note: in means the stripped devil goes inside the affair word

parts.note: a thing is an affair, as in a romantic thing

indicators.note: exposed means the devil loses its outer covering, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A devil revealed in a scandalous affair with sticky fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' means stripped of its outer letters, and 'in' puts what is left inside the affair word.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-fingered describes someone given to petty pilfering, i.e. stealing.

clue.text: Wooden seats in Rose Bowl Stadium

definitions.note: used as an adjective, as in elm furniture

indicators.note: seats are bottoms, so the bottom (last) letters of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: Timber seating at the Rose Bowl, the American football stadium in Pasadena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seats' are bottoms: the last letters of Rose, Bowl and Stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: Used attributively, the tree's name describes things made of its timber, as in an elm chair.

clue.text: Investment product used by Hitachi regularly yields a profit, we're told?

definitions.note: said aloud, 'a profit' sounds like a prophet; this one is a Hebrew prophet

parts.note: an ISA is a UK Individual Savings Account, a tax-free investment product

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of Hitachi, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: An investment scheme used by the electronics firm Hitachi steadily returns a gain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on sound: 'a profit' heard as a prophet, the Old Testament one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament book is named after this Hebrew prophet, a homophone of 'a profit'.

clue.text: Plates overturned by creature

indicators.note: overturned means the plates word is turned over, written backwards

parts.note: laminae, here lamina, are thin plates or layers

explanation.surface: Crockery knocked over by a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses LAMINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living beast is a creature in the general sense.

clue.text: Fail to pick out retro 70s fashion items?

parts.note: to tank is to fail badly

indicators.note: retro means backwards, so the pick-out word is reversed

parts.note: to spot is to pick out

explanation.surface: Failing to identify retro clothing from the seventies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' looks like part of the definition but reverses SPOT into TOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeveless knitted jumpers worn over shirts were a 1970s fashion staple.
